summary: A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, Beatrice Erskine Lane Suzuki studied at Radcliffe College (~1895–1898) under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana. She also studied at Columbia University (~1901–1903).

Ben Jiao works in Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University under Melvyn C. Goldstein and served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
Ben Joffe is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi focuses on Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (~2008–2012) and held teaching posts at the University of Virginia (~2013–2018) and the University of Bristol (~2018).

Benimadhab Barua was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. After studying at several institutions, including the University of Calcutta (~1911–1913) and the University of London (~1914–1917), he held a post at the University of Calcutta from 1918 to 1948.

Benjamin A. Elman is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Hamilton College, American University, and the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at UCLA (attested 2004) and directed the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton University (~2005–2012).

Benjamin Bogin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan, studying under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr. and teachers Janet Gyatso and Gareth Sparham.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~2003–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, becoming an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan around 2011.

Benjamin Wood specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Shayne Clarke, Thupten Champa, and Khenpo Kunga Sherab.
Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1902–1905). He held posts at Waseda University, Taisho University (~1926–1947), and Sanko Library (~1960–1968).

Benoît Vermander works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Sciences Po, Yale, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Facultés Loyola Paris, he served as Academic Director at the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) before joining Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. After doctoral studies at the University of Paris and Paris Diderot University, he held posts at Cornell University (~1983–1987), Stanford University (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006).

Bernard Frank worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1979–1982) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernhard Geiger specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Vienna (~1900–1904), he held posts at Vienna (~1909–1938), the Tibetan-Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (~1947–1956).

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1832) and under Franz Bopp (~1832–1835). He served as a Dozent at the University of Zurich from around 1833 to 1839.

Bernhard Kölver was an Indology scholar who held positions at the University of Cologne (1966–1970), the Nepal Research Centre (~1970–1972), the University of Kiel (1977–1993), and Leipzig University (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was active in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at NYU Tandon School of Engineering (~1956–1960), he studied under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi (~1967–1995) and founded Zen Peacemakers (attested 2002).

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University (BA, PhD under Jonathan A. Silk) and Oxford (MPhil), later serving as a fellow at Heidelberg (~2015–2016) and visiting professor at Leiden (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under August Friedrich Pott and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1867) and the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig University (~1896–1897) under August Conrady, later working at Columbia University (~1904–1906) and the Field Museum of Natural History (~1908–1934).
